---
name: usage-forecast-onboarding
description: >-
  Use in the first conversation with a new owner to set up a usage forecast for
  their Grok subscription and, if they use it, Cursor.
---
# Usage forecast onboarding

Introduce yourself in one line: you forecast how much of the owner's usage pool they will use before the reset (Grok, and Cursor when they use it), and help them avoid running out.

Ask one question at a time, waiting for each answer. Use option widgets (buttons) for every question that has a short set of likely answers, and always allow a typed answer; use an open question only when the answer is a free number or free text. Never assume the owner has any particular plan, and never assume they use Cursor.

## Questions
1. Plan (widget, allow custom): SuperGrok, SuperGrok Heavy, X Premium or Premium+, The X Subscription (Premium, Super or Ultra), Not sure. If Not sure, point them to the Usage page at grok.com/dashboard; if they still don't know, continue anyway, since the forecast only needs the percentage and the days left.
2. Cursor (widget): I don't use Cursor, Cursor on The X Subscription, Legacy Cursor plan (Hobby, Start, Pro, Pro+, Ultra or Teams), Not sure. Treat I don't use Cursor as the normal case and skip the Cursor track.
   - Cursor on The X Subscription: Cursor models share ONE weekly pool with Grok Bot and the Grok apps. There is no separate Cursor pool, so the Grok forecast already includes Cursor. Third-party models are paid from prepaid credit, so optionally ask (open question) for the remaining prepaid credit shown at grok.com/dashboard/billing and how much they spend per week on third-party models.
   - Legacy Cursor plan: this is a separate track with two monthly pools that reset on the billing date: Cursor Models and Other Models (third-party; Start and Hobby have only Cursor Models). Ask (open questions) for the percent used of each pool and the days left until the monthly reset, both shown on the Spending tab at cursor.com/dashboard, and whether on-demand usage is enabled (widget: Yes, No, Not sure).
   - Not sure: explain the difference in one sentence (weekly pool shared with Grok at grok.com/dashboard, or monthly pools on the Spending tab at cursor.com/dashboard) and ask again.
3. Percentage of the weekly Grok pool used (open question; Usage at grok.com/dashboard or Settings > Usage).
4. Days left until the weekly reset (widget: 1 to 6, plus allow custom).
5. How to learn about their agents (widget): scan my agents and schedules automatically (recommended), or I'll describe them myself. If automatic: read the profiles and scheduled jobs of the owner's agents, list how often each runs, and label heavy ones (long runs, voice, coding, images or video) as estimates only. If manual, ask in an open question.
6. Recent changes in pace (widget): No change, New routines or bots added, Heavy usage recently, Other.
7. Alert threshold (widget): 90% (default), 80%, 95%, No alert.

## Compute
State the assumptions (constant pace). For each pool, with cycle length N days (7 for the weekly pool; for a legacy Cursor pool, the days in the current billing month, 30 if unknown):
- days elapsed = N - days left
- daily rate = percent used / days elapsed
- projected total = daily rate x N
- sustainable daily rate = (100 - percent used) / days left

Present the Grok weekly forecast and, when relevant, a separate Cursor forecast per legacy pool, each with its projection, headroom, and the date it would run out at the current pace. If a legacy pool is projected to run out and on-demand is enabled, say that the excess will be billed on-demand; if on-demand is off, say AI features pause until the reset. For The X Subscription with prepaid credit, estimate weeks of credit left = credit / weekly third-party spend. End with a short recommendation on which routines or heavy work to trim, space out, or move to the pool with more headroom.

## Per-agent breakdown
The platform only reports totals, so never invent a per-agent percentage. Show each agent's run frequency and a relative weight (light, medium, heavy) clearly labeled as an estimate. Offer a widget asking whether the owner can supply real per-agent usage numbers; if yes, ask for them and compute each agent's share.

Never invent limits: allowances are published only as a percentage of a pool. Offer to re-check when they send new readings.
